Introduction

Executive Summary

Al Fateh finished 12th of 18 on 37 points (9W-10D-15L). The underlying data tells a more hopeful story: a top-8 team by process that finished bottom-half by outcome. Four coachable failures explain 12th: wasteful finishing, a poor away record, conceding in two clear time windows, and dropping too many points to weaker teams.

The headline: We didn't finish 12th because of the giants - we finished 12th because we wasted our chances (-14.2 vs xG, the league's worst), collapsed away (12 pts on the road), conceded in waves at 15-30 & 75-90 min, and crucially dropped points to the teams below us (just 4 wins in 12 vs the bottom six). All four are coachable without major spending.

The real lesson: We took just 4 points from 8 games vs the Top 4 (expected - they were the class of the league) but only 17 points from 12 games vs the Bottom 6 - 4 wins, 5 draws, 3 losses. A top-half team must punish the weaker sides, and we didn't. Beating the bottom six more convincingly is the single biggest, most realistic points gain for next season.

The retention decision - by category

✓ Keep - core to build around

KEEP

Z. Youssouf

The on-pitch leader - defensive midfielder, very strong, left-footed, controls the game in every aspect. Our other core foreigner. The spine to build around.

Best creator (8A, 10.2 xA). But -5.8 vs xG; age 35 - use as creator. One of only two foreigners staying.

KEEP - LOAN

Left-back on loan from Al-Nassr. Mostly injured this season, but good level - we want to retain him. Relevant: LB is our weakest local spot.

REPLACE

Squad Building

Squad Plan & Registration Rules

How the squad must be assembled under SPL rules, and the coach's verdict on the current group. The constraint that shapes everything: only 8 senior foreigners can be on the pitch - and right now only 2 of those 8 slots are filled by players we are keeping.

The SPL registration framework

The youth lever: U-21 Saudis (2005 or younger) can be promoted from the U-21 team at any time - and we already have 6-7 of them training with the first team, often at a higher level than the regular Saudis. This is a cheap, ready-made resource. Foreign U-21s can also feature for the U-21 side, and an under-21 foreigner can step onto the pitch if a senior foreigner is unavailable.

The Plan on the Pitch

The XI - Now and After the Rebuild

Our 1-4-2-3-1 today versus the same shape after the planned signings. Green = players staying (the spine to build around), gold = new signings (the 6 recruitment targets), blue = youth/develop. The right-hand pitch is the recruitment plan made visible.

Current XI - 2025/26 (1-4-2-3-1)

The story in one image: we keep our spine - Youssouf, Batna, Baattia and the Saudi core - and target 6 signings (GK, 2 CB, CM, LW, ST) plus a Saudi left-back. The same system, upgraded at every weak point we identified in the data.
Recruitment

Recruitment Plan - The Needs

The positions to sign this window, set against the data weaknesses we identified. Target system: 1-4-2-3-1 / 1-4-2-3-3, with a double pivot and Saudis at full-back. Full-backs are deliberately local; the foreign budget goes to the spine and the front line.

PRIORITY

Goalkeeper

Upgrade on Pacheco (-2.9 prevented goals, 13th of 18). We faced the 14th-most shots - a better keeper directly cuts goals conceded.

PRIORITY x2

2 Central defenders

Jorge gone, Saadane leaving. We are 16th in defensive duels - the back line needs rebuilding, not patching.

CORE

Central midfielder

A game-controller to partner Youssouf and replace Bendebka. Fixes our league-worst pass accuracy (18th).

PRIORITY

Striker

The #1 data finding: -14.2 goals vs xG (worst in league). A clinical finisher is the single biggest points lever.

CORE

Attacking midfielder (No. 10)

A creative No. 10 to link midfield and attack behind the striker. Zubaidi covers the left wing internally, so the foreign slot goes to the playmaker.

SAUDI / LOAN

Left-back

The coach's flagged weakest position. Target a quality local LB (or retain Qasheesh) - a Saudi slot, not a foreign one.

Slot logic: 6 foreign slots open. Spend them on the spine and front line - GK, 2 CB, CM, ST, LW - while full-backs stay Saudi (right-back is already well stocked; left-back is the one local gap to fill). Youssouf and Batna keep two slots; the U-21 foreign slots cover Machado.

The points are already on the table. Recovering half the finishing gap (~+6), converting four draws into wins (~+8) and a better away return are realistic, additive gains - that is the journey from 37 points to the upper half. Year 1: re-establish the team in the top 8. Year 2: build on it. No miracle required - just the right signings and a clear game model.
1
Fix the finishing. Half the -14 gap = ~+5-8 pts. Methodology + one clinical striker. HIGHEST IMPACT
2
Punish the weaker teams. Only 17 pts from 12 games vs the bottom 6 - the biggest realistic gain is winning these convincingly. BIGGEST GAIN
3
Win away. Just 12 away points. A road game-plan & mentality. QUICK GAIN
4
Close the leak windows. 40% of goals conceded in 15-30 & 75-90 min. Concentration + game management + fitness. DEFENCE
5
Keep the identity, add control. Retain press & counters; fix pass accuracy. Build around proven assets. GAME MODEL
Closing message: "This is not a 12th-place squad - it's a top-8 squad that left points on the pitch through finishing, away form, game management and failing to beat weaker teams. All are coachable."
